pages.quiz:
FRENCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #11
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: FRENCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Interactive speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Interactive speaking.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive speaking.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Interactive speaking.

2. When practising Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading.

3. When practising Persuasive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Persuasive Speaking.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Persuasive Speaking.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Persuasive Speaking.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Persuasive Speaking.

4. When practising Intensive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Listening.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Listening.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Listening.

5. When practising Critical Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Critical Listening.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Critical Listening.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Critical Listening.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Critical Listening.

6. When practising Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.

7. “Bonjour” is used to say: (1 mark)
   A. Good night only
   B. Good morning / hello
   C. Excuse me
   D. Thank you

8. When practising Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.

9. When practising Reading for information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading for information.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for information.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for information.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading for information.

10. When practising Informative Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Informative Speaking.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Informative Speaking.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Informative Speaking.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Informative Speaking.

11. When practising Listening for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Information.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Information.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Information.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.

12. The French word for “book” is: (1 mark)
   A. chaise
   B. porte
   C. fenêtre
   D. livre

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Critical Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Listening for Information and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking.

2. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading.

3. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Persuasive Speaking.

4. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Listening.

5. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Critical Listening.

6. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.

7. B — Good morning / hello

8. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.

9. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for information.

10. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Informative Speaking.

11. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.

12. D — livre

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Critical Listening; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening for Information; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
